evidence.title: Serve owner-authorized Timeline source previews as safe HTML in the actual Incident-to-Case local browser
evidence.goal: Close the functional gap on the runnable Incident→Case→source browser path: the endpoint opened in the browser still returned JSON. Integrate existing source-identical safe HTML rendering and stronger owner identity checks from independent PR #204 into the pre-existing source-open host in PR #203; preserve both original PR SHAs and full JSON compatibility.
outputs: Read-only browser Incident→Case Timeline→source preview rendered as HTML on the existing route, with independent owner read and safe return navigation
Source-identical #204 HTML/core security tests plus actual #203 loopback HTTP browser end-to-end for HTML/JSON positive and both-format negative authorization
Reconciled integration path without changing frozen #203/#204, inherited modern Go/SCA gate from #203
acceptance_tests: Actual first-party Go httptest starts the runnable loopback front door, follows authorized Incident→Case source URL with native Accept:text/html and sees escaped preview plus no-store/CSP
Same URL with Accept:application/json still returns original JSON and no HTML
Anonymous, Command-only, foreign Case/Entry, forged sourceRef or invalid Basic password receive no protected preview in either Accept mode
Corrupt canonical source object identity/reference denied; source HTML/JSON is not partially emitted after cancellation
CI on exact HEAD passes 3 platforms, Go race/vet, engineering kernel SAST/SCA including govulncheck. Security failure must not be waived.

rules: Strict tenant isolation and permission checking
